source.title: An Investigation into Neural Net Optimization via Hessian Eigenvalue Density
source.authors: B. Ghorbani; Shankar Krishnan; Ying Xiao

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present, including appendices.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures Hessian spectra and gradient alignment during training and compares batch-normalization settings, reporting findings about optimization geometry that bear on V7's sharpness/generalization-gap relation. It does not measure the generalization gap itself.
record.gate_note: The study measures Hessian spectra and gradient concentration, but reports no test-error/generalization-gap comparison among the measured networks. The cited claims from other work are not rows. Measurements in Sections 3–4 are included only when they are relevant to a mapped claim; the reported BN training-speed result is not itself a generalization-gap result.
record.test_reason: The study measures Hessian spectra, gradient concentration, and optimization speed, without testing any listed version. In particular, it does not compare magnitude-aware sharpness with training–test gaps as V7 requires. Appendix F reports validation accuracies, but does not pair them with sharpness measurements or provide a relevant controlled comparison.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate, but the proposed mechanism should retain its status as a hypothesis supported by experiments and quadratic analysis. The authors report that batch normalization suppresses Hessian outliers and gradient concentration, and argue that these effects explain faster optimization. They do not establish a relationship between these properties and generalization gaps.
record.recipe_differences: The paper estimates full Hessian spectra and studies optimization geometry and batch normalization. It does not reproduce the generalization-gap measurement or magnitude-aware perturbation comparison described in V7.
record.method_sensitivity: Batch normalization presence and normalization statistics (mini-batch versus population); architecture comparisons include ResNet and VGG, but no generalization-gap outcome is reported for these conditions.

fits_no_version.finding: Batch normalization suppresses isolated Hessian eigenvalues and reduces gradient concentration in their eigenspaces; population-statistics normalization restores outliers and slows optimization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Batch normalization can accelerate optimization by suppressing Hessian outliers and associated gradient concentration.

fits_no_version.finding: The Hessian spectrum contracts after a learning-rate decrease and when residual connections are removed in the reported ResNet-32 comparisons (Section 3, Figures 4–5). Neither comparison measures generalization gaps.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Learning-rate and residual-connection changes can affect Hessian curvature contrary to common optimization-landscape intuitions.

record.problems: No generalization gap or test-error comparisons are reported for the measured Hessian properties. The authors state their experiments do not conclusively prove or refute the broader hypotheses discussed.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible result rows: measured Hessian and gradient properties are not paired with the generalization-gap outcome required by V7 or another listed version. Training-speed and spectrum comparisons do not by themselves measure that outcome.

untested.parts: Random-label memorization and held-out performance under matched natural- and random-label training.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD on held-out performance under specified tuning budgets.
Batch-size effects on held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance versus generalization gaps among similarly fitted networks, including comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
Test-accuracy effects of removing memorized examples versus random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: Change the record's tests/T2 classification to discusses/T6 and V7 from tested_not_extracted to not tested. Full-batch versus mini-batch normalization statistics is not a training-batch-size comparison testing V5. The empty row set is appropriate; the related optimization findings are already covered by rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural versus random labels.
Width sweep and test error beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected test error and effects of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizer versus SGD held-out performance.
Large- versus small-batch held-out performance under epoch budgets.

The paper measures Hessian spectral properties and training dynamics but does not report the generalization gaps, weight-magnitude-scaled perturbation measure, or comparison to norm- and margin-based measures specified in V7.
Removal and retraining of memorized examples and resulting test accuracy.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
